Subject: Custody windows and secure handback — order form details

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the demo last week — SoundWave is very interested in moving forward but our compliance team needs clarity on two items for the order form:

1) Custody/processing window options: we need explicit language that data processed in the EU region can be configured with bespoke custody windows (e.g., ephemeral session-only, 30/90/180 day persistence) depending on the dataset class.
2) Secure handback (decommission) timelines: in the event of contract termination or migration, we need certifiable deletion + evidence within a defined SLA (we typically ask for certs within 30 days; some regulated data may need a faster path).

Can you share the standard order form language you propose and any operational constraints (e.g., longest practicable deletion chain across caches, backups, and analytics derivatives)? Also, any attachments we should expect in the RFP response (dataflow diagram, deletion certificate template)?

Appreciate a short Q&A or a concrete snippet we can add to our procurement checklist.

Best,

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear list. TL;DR: we can offer configurable custody windows and a certified deletion workflow; below is the proposed order form language plus a summary of operational constraints. I attached a first-draft order form and a simple handback dataflow diagram for context.

Proposed order form snippet (editable):
- Data Residency: Customer data will be processed and stored in the EU region unless Customer configures otherwise.
- Retention Windows (customer-selectable per dataset class): Ephemeral (session-only, auto-purge within 24h), Short (30 days), Standard (90 days), Extended (180 days).
- Deletion & Handback: Upon contract termination or written request, Redwood will: (a) initiate deletion of primary storage and KV caches within X hours; (b) purge backups in the next scheduled retention cycle; (c) provide a Deletion Certificate within 30 days certifying primary and cache erasure. For regulated datasets requiring expedited erasure, Redwood offers an accelerated handback (target: certificate within 7 days) as an add-on.

Operational notes / constraints:
- Caches: KV caches and prefix caches are cleared immediately on request, but in-flight requests may reference cached tokens until flush completion (typical flush < 2 hours for targeted namespaces).
- Backups: backup deletion depends on backup cadence. For daily backups our standard policy is to remove from active backup sets on next cycle; we guarantee backup purging and certification within 30 days by default.
- Analytics/derivatives: aggregated analytics that do not contain PII can be retained for product improvement unless specifically requested for deletion; derivatives containing customer-identifiable data are included in deletion scopes.

Attachments: draft-orderform-soundwave-v1.pdf (order form snippet), dataflow-handback-diagram.png (high-level handback flow).

Next steps: Monica (legal) and Vivek (ops) are cc'd to confirm legal phrasing and operational feasibility. If that looks acceptable, we can translate this into an order form line item and add the accelerated-handback add-on to the SOW. Also happy to jump on a 30-minute call if you prefer.

Cheers,

Thanks Stephanie / Aisha — quick legal clarifications:

- "Deletion Certificate" language: we use a standard certificate that lists the scopes (primary storage, caches, backups, indices, log indices) and the date/time each scope was sanitized. We can deliver the certificate as a signed PDF within the agreed SLA window.
- "Accelerated handback" (7-day cert) is permitted but requires: (1) customer-provided confirmation of dataset classes to accelerate; (2) a short runbook for any archive restores that would otherwise block backup trimming; and (3) a one-time operational fee to cover expedited backup pruning and verification.
- Be explicit about derivatives: the order form should include a checkbox where customers can elect to include product analytics/derivatives in the deletion scope.

I'll attach the standard deletion certificate template to the SOW after we agree the windows.

Subject: Re: Custody windows and secure handback — order form details

Operational detail from infra/ops perspective:

- Immediate actions: for any handback request we will: (1) isolate the tenant namespace; (2) flush runtime caches for that namespace (typical completion <2 hours for micro-busts); (3) disable any further persistent writes.
- Primary storage deletion: objects and indexes removed within 24-72 hours depending on dataset volume; small customers (<1TB) typically see completion in 24h; large datasets will be scheduled with a rolling delete to avoid runtime impact.
- Backups & archive: as Monica notes, backup pruning follows backup cadence. For daily backups we mark candidate snapshots and remove them on next cycle — certification then follows. Accelerated purging requires a snapshot traverse and verification step that is manual and subject to a one-time operational fee.
- Evidence & audit logs: we can provide a machine-readable deletion manifest (CSV) plus a signed PDF certificate. We also capture audit traces showing user-initiated delete events and job-run completion.

Constraints: we cannot guarantee physical media-level forensic wiping (e.g., hardware decommission) within the 30-day certificate window for air-gapped or on-prem customer-managed infrastructure; that should be handled via the customer's own hardware disposition processes or an add-on service.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Operations | Redwood Inference
